title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
domain: math reasoning, scientific QA, instruction following, medical QA, scientific coding

headline_result.text: Across 16 GPT-6 Astra editing trajectories on Qwen3.5-0.8B/9B, held-out gains reached +29.45 (MATH-500), +4.42 (GPQA Diamond), +36.72 (IFEval) and +17.11 (SciBench) points on the 0.8B model, with the MATH gain from changing 1,023 parameters; gains at 9B were small and six trajectories kept the original weights.
headline_result.quote: On full held-out evaluations, accuracy improves by up to 29.45, 4.42, 36.72, and 17.11 percentage points on MATH-500, GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench, respectively. Notably, modifying only 1,023 parameters yields a 29.45-point improvement.

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: single trajectory per model-benchmark pair, except 3 for 0.8B MATH; final evaluation with seed 0

key_claims.claim: Three independent MATH searches on Qwen3.5-0.8B gave very different held-out gains (+29.45, +5.00, +27.30), all editing the layer-23 MLP down-projection.
key_claims.quote: the primary search achieves a +29.45 percentage-point improvement, while reruns 1 and 2 yield gains of +5.00 and +27.30 points, respectively.

key_claims.claim: In six of 16 trajectories the editor kept the original weights, and the evaluated 9B Math candidate lowered held-out accuracy despite a large development gain.
key_claims.quote: Notably, the evaluated 9B Math candidate decreases held-out accuracy by 0.35 points, despite a +29.69-point development gain.

key_claims.claim: A Math-edited 0.8B checkpoint transferred to other benchmarks without further editing, but transfer was uneven.
key_claims.quote: A Math-edited checkpoint improves GPQA Diamond, IFEval, and SciBench by 3.03, 12.18, and 20.10 points, respectively, without further editing, while leaving SciCode performance unchanged.

key_claims.claim: The primary MATH edit subtracts a 'doubt versus progress' token-readout direction (Wait/However/But... vs Therefore/Thus/So...) from one column, targeting reasoning loops; at diagnosis 111 of 128 base samples hit the token cap.
key_claims.quote: On F1 the base model answers 19 of 128 samples correctly, and 111 samples hit the token cap, which points to long, unresolved reasoning as the main failure.

key_claims.claim: On one 48-question batch the chosen edit beat an ablation and a single equal-norm random orthogonal direction (20 vs 4 vs 10 of 48, base 6).
key_claims.quote: and a single random direction orthogonal to u with equal norm gives 10 of 48. On this batch, the chosen intervention outperforms both the ablation and the single equal-norm orthogonal random control.

key_claims.claim: Gains were much smaller at 9B, which already scores 97.70% on MATH-500.
key_claims.quote: The results suggest that smaller models offer greater opportunities for measurable improvements, while stronger models present a more constrained search landscape.

limitations_stated.text: Within a 50-request budget the agent may fail to discover and validate an effective intervention.
limitations_stated.quote: within a fixed exploration budget, the agent may fail to discover and validate an intervention sufficiently effective to justify modifying the original model.

limitations_stated.text: Development gains do not always carry over to held-out data, and evaluation is costly.
limitations_stated.quote: However, development gains do not always translate into reliable held-out improvements, and repeated evaluations incur substantial computational costs.

limitations_stated.text: Development results are adaptively selected without multiple-comparison correction.
limitations_stated.quote: Development results are selected adaptively and are reported without correction for multiple comparisons.

notes_for_review: An independent re-run of MIT's setup (GPT-6 Astra editing Qwen3.5-0.8B, same sampling with presence penalty 1.5 and thinking on, 32k tokens) that roughly reproduces the MATH-500 jump (8.35 to 37.80, versus MIT's 7.9 to 48.1) and extends it to six more benchmarks and a 9B model. Large gains appear only where the small model fails by looping or truncating (base 8.35% MATH, 1.38% SciBench), and the primary edit is a hand-built anti-'Wait' direction, which points to loop suppression rather than new capability; there is no fine-tuning, decoding-setting (e.g. thinking off, token budget) or mechanical edit baseline, and held-out results come from one trajectory and one evaluation seed each. Run-to-run variance (+5.00 to +29.45 on the same task) is reported openly.
